## 14-item checklist

1. **SECRETS** – OK (`.env`, `checkout/index.ts`, `stripe-webhook/index.ts`): Only `VITE_`-prefixed public keys reach the browser. `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are read exclusively from Deno's server-side environment.

2. **DATABASE ACCESS** – ISSUE (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`): All four tables have RLS (Row-Level Security — a database rule that decides which rows a given user is allowed to see) enabled with appropriate policies. However, the storage read policy (`client files read`) contains no per-user restriction, so any authenticated user can generate a signed URL for any file path in the bucket.

3. **AUTHORIZATION** – OK (`checkout/index.ts`, `stripe-webhook/index.ts`): The checkout function validates the caller's JWT (a signed login token) before querying. The webhook verifies Stripe's signature before writing. RLS enforces record-level ownership on every table.

4. **INPUT** – ISSUE (`src/pages/Files.jsx`): File-type and size validation runs only in the browser and can be bypassed by any user who makes the request directly. No equivalent check exists server-side or in a storage policy.

5. **PAYMENTS** – OK (`checkout/index.ts`, `stripe-webhook/index.ts`): Prices come from the `services` table, never from the browser. The webhook signature is verified with `constructEventAsync`. An idempotent upsert on `stripe_session` prevents double-crediting the same payment.

6. **AI/LLM** – NOT APPLICABLE: No AI or large-language-model features are present.

7. **RATE LIMITS & ABUSE** – ISSUE (`checkout/index.ts`): No rate limiting (a cap on how many times one user can hit an endpoint in a given window) is applied to the checkout Edge Function (a small server-side program running in Supabase's cloud).

8. **HEADERS & CORS** – ISSUE: No security headers (`Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, etc.) or CORS configuration (a rule that controls which websites can call your API) is visible in any file.

9. **DATA EXPOSURE** – OK: The checkout function returns only a redirect URL. RLS on `bookings` and `messages` limits responses to the caller's own rows. `services` is intentionally public. React escapes all rendered text, so `sender_name` and `body` in messages cannot inject HTML.

10. **DESTRUCTIVE OPS** – OK: No DELETE policies exist for any user-facing table. No admin actions are reachable through any client-side route.

11. **FILE STORAGE** – ISSUE (`001_init.sql`): The `client-files` bucket is correctly set to `public: false` and files are served through 60-second expiring links, but the read policy does not scope access to the requesting user's own folder — same vulnerability as item 2.

12. **ROLES** – OK (`001_init.sql`): Roles are stored in a server-side database table. No INSERT or UPDATE policy exists for ordinary users; only the service role (a privileged server credential that bypasses RLS) can write to that table. Uploaded files could contain identity documents or receipts — already protected by a private bucket and expiring links. Confirm with a lawyer whether your jurisdiction's privacy law (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) requires a formal record of what personal data you hold and why.

---

## 1. Stack Decision

> **About your build tool:** Lovable generates a React (Vite) front end and connects it to Supabase for the database, authentication, and server-side code. Several rows below are "decided for you" by that combination — noted where relevant.

| Layer | Choice | Why | Rejected alternative & why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | React + Vite | Lovable decides this — no choice needed | — |
| **Backend / API** | Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) — *serverless functions: short-lived pieces of code that run on Supabase's servers instead of your computer or a traditional server* | Lovable's built-in server layer; $0; required so secrets and business logic never run in the browser | AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Workers — not integrated with Lovable out of the box |
| **Database** | Supabase Postgres | Comes with Supabase; includes Row-Level Security (*RLS — database rules that say which logged-in user is allowed to read or change which rows, enforced by the database itself, not just your code*); $0 | PlanetScale, Neon — extra account, extra cost, no added benefit here |
| **Auth** | Supabase Auth | Built into Supabase; supports custom JWT claims (*a JWT is a signed digital badge the server issues; "custom claims" let us stamp a role like "owner" or "helper" onto it so the database can enforce permissions automatically*); $0 | Auth0, Clerk — paid at meaningful scale |
| **File storage** | None (V1) | No file uploads in spec | Supabase Storage — add later if you want menu photos |
| **Payments** | Square Hosted Checkout | Spec requires Square; the "hosted" page means Square's website collects the card number, not yours — your code never sees it | Stripe — not in spec |
| **AI / LLM** | None | Not in spec | — |
| **Hosting** | Lovable's built-in publishing | Lovable hosts the React app automatically; $0 | Vercel, Netlify — extra account for no gain when Lovable already does it |
| **SMS notifications** | Twilio | Most straightforward pay-per-message SMS API; $15 free credit to start | AWS SNS — harder to set up; MessageBird — smaller community, less documentation |

> **SMS is not truly $0.** Twilio charges roughly **$0.008 per text** in the US. More importantly, US law requires businesses to register their texting use with the phone carriers — called **A2P 10DLC registration** (*"A2P" means Application-to-Person; "10DLC" means a standard 10-digit US phone number*). That registration costs about **$4 one-time + $10–15/month** and takes **5–7 business days**. Start it on Day 1. ## 2. System Diagram

> Arrows show which direction data flows. "UNTRUSTED" means anyone in the world can look at the code running there. "TRUSTED" means only Supabase's servers run that code, and users can't read or modify it.

- **Twilio API calls** — sending SMS
- **`customer_phone` retrieval** — full phone number never leaves the server except to the Owner
- **Order total calculation** — server fetches current `price_cents` from `MenuItem`, ignores any price sent by the browser
- **Slot availability check with row lock** — a Postgres function uses `SELECT FOR UPDATE` (*a database instruction that locks the slot row for a fraction of a second so two simultaneous orders can't both claim the last spot*) and either reserves the slot or returns "full"
- **Hold expiry cleanup** — a `pg_cron` job (*a built-in Supabase scheduler — like a timer that runs a database command on a schedule*) runs every minute: `UPDATE orders SET status = 'expired' WHERE status = 'hold' AND hold_expires_at < now()`
- **Payment webhook verification** — Square signs each webhook with a secret key; the Edge Function checks the signature before trusting the "payment succeeded" message
- **Role enforcement** — JWT claims are set by a Postgres hook function that runs on every login and reads from a server-side `user_roles` table

|---|---|---|---|

| Customer | No login; `private_token` UUID in URL | Not stored as a role — the token is looked up in the `orders` table | N/A — they have no account |

When writing Lovable prompts, include the instruction: *"This logic must be in a Supabase Edge Function — do not query this data directly from the React component."*

The Supabase **anon key** being visible in the browser is expected and safe — it only unlocks what RLS permits. The **service role key** (*a master key that bypasses all RLS rules*) must only ever exist in Edge Function environment variables and must never appear in any frontend file.

Supabase Auth's JavaScript library stores the Owner and Helper session in `localStorage` by default (*the browser's built-in key-value storage — readable by any JavaScript on the page*). # ARCHITECTURE.md — How the App Is Actually Built

## Stack

| Layer | Technology | Plain-English description |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend | React + Vite | A JavaScript UI framework compiled to static files and served from a CDN (content delivery network — a globally distributed file server) |
| Database | Supabase / PostgreSQL | A hosted relational database; every table uses **Row Level Security (RLS)** — rules baked into the database itself that decide which rows each user may see or change |
| Authentication | Supabase Auth | Manages sign-up, sign-in, and the JWT (JSON Web Token — a signed credential the browser carries to prove who the user is) |
| File storage | Supabase Storage | An S3-compatible private file store; access is controlled by RLS policies on `storage.objects` |
| Edge Functions | Supabase / Deno | Small server-side programs that run in the cloud close to users; the only place secret keys live |
| Payments | Stripe Checkout + Webhooks | Stripe hosts the payment page; a **webhook** is an HTTP callback Stripe sends to your server when an event (like a completed payment) occurs |

## Trust Boundaries

| What runs here | Location | Secrets present |
|---|---|---|
| React UI | **Browser** | `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — intentionally public; security comes from RLS, not key secrecy |
| Supabase DB / Auth / Storage | **Supabase servers** | Service role key (never sent to browser) |
| `checkout` Edge Function | **Deno / Supabase servers** | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` |
| `stripe-webhook` Edge Function | **Deno / Supabase servers** | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` |

**Price trust boundary:** The browser sends only a `serviceId` string. The `checkout` function reads `price_cents` from the database. Stripe is told the price by the server. The client can never inflate or deflate the amount charged.

**Webhook trust boundary:** The `stripe-webhook` function calls `stripe.webhooks.constructEventAsync` which cryptographically verifies the `stripe-signature` header using `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. A forged request cannot create a booking.

1. No server-side file type or size enforcement — only the browser validates
2. `sender_name` in messages is free text; any user can claim any display name
3. New users receive no automatic role assignment; their role state is undefined
4. Staff and admin roles exist in the schema but unlock no extra data access inside the app
5. No rate limiting on message inserts or file uploads
6. No CORS (cross-origin) origin restriction on Edge Functions
7. Health data (intake forms, free-text messages) stored without a formal data-handling policy

## In Plain English

- **Your Stripe secret key never leaves the server.** The browser only ever sees a redirect URL, not the key used to create it.
- **The database enforces its own access rules.** Even if someone wrote a script to query your database directly, the Row Level Security rules would still block them from seeing anyone else's bookings or files.
- **Files are locked in private folders.** Each client's uploads sit in their own folder and can only be opened with a short-lived link that expires in 60 seconds.
- **The webhook is the only thing that marks a booking as paid.** Stripe's signature check means a fake "payment completed" message can't trick your server into confirming a free booking.
- **Staff and admin exist on paper but not in the app.** The roles are recorded in the database, but the app gives them the same view as any client — an admin UI still needs to be built.

# SPEC.md — What the App Does Today

## One-liner
Cleanbook is a single-studio booking site where authenticated clients pay for a massage service, upload their intake form, and exchange messages with the studio.

---

## Users & Roles

| Role | Can do today | **Must NEVER do** |
|---|---|---|
| **Visitor** (not logged in) | Browse the public service and price list | See any booking, message, or file belonging to anyone |
| **Client** (logged in) | Book and pay for a service; upload and view their own intake files; send and read messages with the studio; view their own bookings | See another client's bookings, files, or messages; write a booking record directly to the database without paying; change their own role; claim someone else's name on a message *(currently violated — see Gap List)* |
| **Staff** | Identical to Client in current code — no distinct permissions exist | View any client's private data; modify or cancel bookings; change any user's role |
| **Admin** | Full data access and management | Be locked out; accidentally wipe all booking records |

---

## The Core Loop

1. **Discover** — visitor browses available services and prices (no login required).
2. **Log in** — client authenticates via Supabase Auth.
3. **Book** — client clicks "Book and pay"; the browser calls the `checkout` Edge Function (a small piece of server-side code that runs outside the browser); the function looks up the real price in the database and creates a Stripe-hosted payment page.
4. **Pay** — client completes payment on Stripe's own page and is redirected to `/done`.
5. **Confirm** — Stripe sends a webhook (an automatic server-to-server notification) to the `stripe-webhook` Edge Function; after verifying Stripe's digital signature, the function creates a `bookings` row with `status = 'paid'`.
6. **Intake** — client uploads their intake form (PDF, PNG, or JPG, ≤ 5 MB) to their private storage folder.
7. **Communicate** — client and admin exchange text messages (≤ 2,000 characters each).

---

## Features That Exist (with Testable Acceptance Criteria)

| Feature | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|
| **Public service list** | A visitor with no account can query the `services` table and receive all rows including `name` and `price_cents`. |
| **Book & pay (checkout)** | An authenticated client POSTs `{ serviceId }` to the `checkout` function; the function returns a Stripe session URL; the Stripe page shows the correct service name and price from the database (not from the browser). |
| **Payment confirmation webhook** | After Stripe fires `checkout.session.completed`, a row in `bookings` contains `status='paid'`, the correct `user_id`, `service_id`, and `stripe_session`; sending the same webhook event a second time does not create a duplicate row (the `upsert` with `onConflict: 'stripe_session'` handles this). *Upsert — a database write that inserts a new row or updates the existing one if it already exists.* |
| **File upload** | A logged-in client uploads a PDF/PNG/JPG ≤ 5 MB; it is stored at `client-files/{user_id}/{uuid}`; a second authenticated user cannot read or list it. |
| **Signed file link** | Calling `openFile(path)` generates a URL that opens the file in a new tab; the URL stops working after 60 seconds. *Signed URL — a temporary link with a cryptographic token baked in, granting access to a private file for a limited time without needing a login.* |
| **Messaging** | A logged-in user can insert a message where `from_id` equals their own user ID and `body` is ≤ 2,000 characters; both the sender and the recipient (matched by UUID) can read it; a third party cannot. |
| **Role read-back** | A logged-in user can read their own row in `user_roles`; they cannot read another user's row; they cannot insert or update any row. |

## Edge Cases NOT Handled

- **No time or slot selection.** Clients pay for a service type without choosing a date or time. There is no availability calendar, no conflict detection, and no scheduled-date column in `bookings`. Double-booking is trivially possible.
- **No cancellation or refund flow.** Only `checkout.session.completed` is handled. `charge.refunded`, `checkout.session.expired`, and `payment_intent.payment_failed` are silently ignored; `bookings` rows are never updated or removed.
- **No booking confirmation email or SMS.** Clients receive no app-generated notification after payment (only Stripe's built-in receipt, if configured).
- **No admin or staff UI.** Staff and admin log in to the same screens as clients and can only see their own personal data through the app. Managing the business requires direct Supabase dashboard access.
- **`sender_name` is free text, not derived from the user's profile.** Anyone can write any name when inserting a message. (Also listed in Gap List because it is currently exploitable.)
- **No automatic role assignment on sign-up.** New users have no row in `user_roles`. Any future code that branches on role will receive `null`.
- **`staff` role has no distinct permissions.** The enum value exists; no RLS policy or Edge Function grants staff any elevated access over a regular client.
- **No `profiles` table.** There is no canonical store for display names, phone numbers, or contact details.
- **Client can message any UUID.** The `to_id` field is not restricted to the admin's UUID; a client who knows another user's UUID could send them messages.
- **No pagination on messages or bookings.** All rows are returned on every query; page performance degrades as volume grows.
- **Admin cannot access client files through the app.** There is no storage RLS policy granting admin or staff access to any client's folder; they must use the Supabase dashboard with elevated credentials.
- **No intake-form content validation.** Any file with the right extension is accepted; there is no check that the content is actually an intake form.
- **Multiple Stripe sessions per service.** A client can initiate multiple checkout sessions for the same service; there is no per-client-per-service limit, and abandoned sessions stay open until they expire.
- **No CORS handling visible on Edge Functions.** If Supabase does not automatically inject CORS headers for custom functions, browser preflight requests (*the browser's automatic "permission check" before a cross-origin request*) to the `checkout` function may fail silently.
- **Messages are immutable from the app.** Neither client nor admin can edit or delete a message through the app.

## Known Risks

1. **`sender_name` is unvalidated.** Any authenticated client can insert a message claiming to be "Admin" or any other name. (Detail in Gap List.)
2. **File type enforcement is browser-only.** Storage RLS checks folder ownership, not MIME type or file size.
3. **No staff or admin database policies.** The `role` enum exists and is correctly stored, but no RLS policy grants staff or admin any additional read/write access through the app.
4. **No sign-up trigger.** New users are never given a default row in `user_roles`; future role-based logic would receive `null`.
5. **Service-role key scope.** Any future Edge Function that imports `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` silently bypasses all RLS. The blast radius of a mistake here is the entire database.
6. **No CORS handling visible.** Edge Functions may need an explicit `OPTIONS` handler to serve browser preflight requests.

## In Plain English

- **The browser is untrusted.** Everything rendered in a user's browser can be modified by that user. The database's RLS rules and the server-side Edge Functions are where security actually lives.
- **The anon key and Supabase URL are public on purpose.** Think of them as the hotel's street address and lobby door code — you still need a personal key card (your login JWT) to open your own room.
- **Payments never touch this app's code.** Users are redirected to Stripe's own page to enter card details; the app only learns the outcome ("paid" or "not paid") after Stripe sends a verified notification.
- **The booking record is only created after Stripe proves the payment is real.** The webhook checks Stripe's cryptographic signature before writing anything; there is no way for a browser to fake that signature.
- **The master database key lives only on Supabase's servers.** It bypasses every access rule. It is used correctly in two places today (the checkout function and the webhook). It must never appear in the browser or in the `.env` file.

# GAP LIST — Ranked by Risk

> Ratings follow this rule: **Critical or High** only when I can name the exact file and line *and* describe what an attacker concretely gains. Missing hardening that exposes nothing on its own (rate limits, security headers, browser-side checks the server already enforces) is **Medium or Low**. Missing features and unhandled edge cases are listed under SPEC.md's "Edge Cases NOT Handled," not here.

---

### 🔴 HIGH — `sender_name` impersonation in messages

| | |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | High |
| **Risk in plain English** | Any logged-in client can send a message that displays as "Admin," "Your Therapist," or any other name, because the database policy does not check the `sender_name` field at all — only the `from_id`. The Messages screen renders this forged name prominently in bold, making social engineering straightforward. |
| **Exact location** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — the `"send as yourself"` INSERT policy: `with check (auth.uid() = from_id)` — validates only `from_id`; `sender_name` is completely unconstrained. `Messages.jsx` line 4 then displays the forged name: `<b>{m.sender_name}</b>`. |
| **What an attacker gains** | An authenticated client can insert a row with `sender_name = 'Admin'` (or the studio owner's real name). Anyone reading that thread — including the real admin — sees the studio's own name attributed to a message the studio never sent, enabling fraudulent instructions, fake rebooking requests, or phishing links that appear to come from the studio. |

**Fix direction:** Remove `sender_name` from the table. Derive the display name server-side from `auth.users` or a `profiles` table at read time, or add a database constraint: `check (sender_name = (select email from auth.users where id = from_id))` combined with an RLS policy that also validates the name field.

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM — File type and size enforcement is browser-only

| | |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Risk in plain English** | An attacker using `curl` or any HTTP tool can bypass the JavaScript checks and upload any file type — including HTML or SVG files with embedded scripts — to their private folder. |
| **Exact location** | `src/pages/Files.jsx` lines 3–5 — the only type/size gate: `if (!ALLOWED.includes(file.type) \|\| file.size > 5_000_000)`. `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — the `"own folder write"` storage policy checks only folder ownership, not MIME type or object size. |
| **What an attacker gains** | Arbitrary files can be stored in the `client-files` bucket. Because files are served via signed URLs from Supabase's storage domain (not `cleanbook.app`), script execution would not affect the app's own origin — but an SVG with embedded JavaScript served from a legitimate Supabase URL is a credible phishing vector, and very large uploads waste storage quota. |

**Fix direction:** Add a Supabase storage policy condition on `content-type` metadata, or validate the file's actual magic bytes (first few bytes that identify file format) inside an Edge Function before accepting the upload.

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM — No rate limiting on the `checkout` Edge Function

| | |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Risk in plain English** | An authenticated user can call the checkout function hundreds of times per minute, flooding Stripe's API with open sessions and potentially hitting Stripe's rate limits, which would prevent real customers from checking out. |
| **Exact location** | `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts` — the entire file; every request immediately executes `stripe.checkout.sessions.create` with no counter, cooldown, or quota check. |
| **What an attacker gains** | Denial-of-service against the checkout flow for other users; inflated Stripe API usage; session clutter that complicates payment reconciliation. |

**Fix direction:** Track session creation count per user per minute in a Redis store or a `rate_limits` table, and return HTTP 429 when the threshold is exceeded.

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM — No database indexes on high-frequency RLS filter columns

| | |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Risk in plain English** | At ten times the current number of users, the queries that fetch a user's own bookings and messages will scan every row in the table instead of jumping directly to the matching rows, causing page loads to slow down badly as data accumulates. |
| **Exact location** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no `CREATE INDEX` statement appears anywhere in the migration; `bookings.user_id`, `messages.from_id`, and `messages.to_id` are unindexed despite being the columns in every user-facing RLS policy. |
| **What an attacker gains** | Not an attacker risk — a scalability risk. A spike in users or bookings degrades the entire app's response time. |

**Fix direction:** Add `CREATE INDEX ON bookings(user_id)`, `CREATE INDEX ON messages(from_id)`, and `CREATE INDEX ON messages(to_id)`.

---

### 🟢 LOW — `.env` file is likely committed to the repository

| | |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | Low |
| **Risk in plain English** | The current `.env` values are intentionally public, but committing a `.env` file to version control normalises the pattern; a future developer could add a real secret to the same file and inadvertently publish it in the repository's history forever. |
| **Exact location** | `.env` — no `.gitignore` was included in the handover; if this file is tracked by git, the habit is established. |
| **What an attacker gains** | Nothing today (values are public). Risk is entirely future-facing: once a secret is in git history, rotating the key is not enough — the history must also be scrubbed. |

**Fix direction:** Add `.env` to `.gitignore`; store the public Supabase values in a `.env.example` with placeholder text; document that real secrets are managed only through Supabase's function-secrets UI.

---

### 🟢 LOW — No sign-up trigger to assign a default role

| | |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | Low |
| **Risk in plain English** | New users are not automatically given a `client` role; any future code that reads `user_roles` to make an access decision will see `null` and could silently fall back to an unintended permission level. |
| **Exact location** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no `CREATE TRIGGER` or `CREATE FUNCTION` exists to insert a default role row when a new user is created in `auth.users`. |
| **What an attacker gains** | No direct attack path today, because no production code currently branches on roles. Risk becomes High the moment a future feature uses `user_roles` for access control decisions without a null-guard. |

**Fix direction:** Add a Postgres trigger on `auth.users` that inserts `('client')` into `user_roles` for every new user, or perform this insert inside the sign-up Edge Function / callback.
